text:
Nora (Sales): FYI Acme demo just started a burst and we're seeing a bunch of 5xxs. They're on the paid POC. Can someone triage? They're also asking what happens to pricing if we switch to a cheaper model fallback.
Ravi (Support): Looking now. Do we have a request id or sample logs from their client?
Nora (Sales): They pasted this in the call: x-req-id=acme-req-3345, code=503, message=service_unavailable. Happening around 11:02 PT. They said traffic spiked from 50r/s -> 400r/s in 3 mins.
Liam (SRE): Thanks. Early guess: burstpool exhaustion + autoscale delay. Checking cluster metrics.
autoscale-bot: autoscaler: scale_up requested (policy=cpu/queue), estimated_ready=36s, pool=shared-burst
Ravi (Support): Can you share the failing response body?
Nora (Sales): Short body: {"error":"503","detail":"no available workers"}
Janet (SE): If we failover to the smaller-cpu model variant (redwood-small-v1) we preserve throughput but increase token latency. Cost per token ~0.5x. Might be a good quick fallback.
Liam (SRE): Metrics: burstpool available tokens=0, queued_requests=980, avg_latency=1.2s. Autoscale fired but nodes pending allocation, cloud provisioning ~40s.
Ravi (Support): For immediate relief, we can enable model-fallback routing (route to compatible quantized variant) and open a temporary ingress throttle for non-critical routes.
Nora (Sales): Customer wants to know: will fallback affect billing? They're concerned about unexpected charges.
Janet (SE): Fallback to redwood-small-v1 would reduce per-token cost; total spend depends on token volume. We can provide an estimate: ~45% lower unit cost given their token mix.
Ravi (Support): I'll propose this to the customer: 1) Enable fallback to small model for 5xxs 2) Short-term credit for the spike (ops discretionary) 3) Follow-up with dedicated capacity quote. @Nora thoughts?
Nora (Sales): Sounds good. They asked for a one-pager on tradeoffs: latency, quality, cost. Can you draft quick bullet points?
Janet (SE): Drafted bullets:
- redwood-large-v1: best quality, highest unit cost, lower latency at high batch sizes
- redwood-small-v1: ~45% lower token cost, slightly higher latency, minor quality delta on long-context prompts
- Fallback behavior: automatic routing on 5xx/timeout; no change to customer API keys
- Recommended: enable fallback + 48hr monitoring window, then evaluate dedicated pool
Ravi (Support): Implemented temporary routing change: fallback enabled for policy=poc-acme, start time=now. Also increased request queue cap to 1500 for that tenant. Watching logs.
autoscale-bot: node-provisioning: 3 nodes requested, status=pending -> provisioning -> ready (ETA 28s)
Liam (SRE): Nodes landing. We'll see queue drain once nodes register. If still failing after 2 min, we'll shift traffic to eu-west region as a last resort.
Ravi (Support): Update: queue length dropping, 503s down to <1% of requests. Sending note to customer. @Nora, recommend offering a one-time POC credit for the spike — helps sales stick the landing.
Nora (Sales): Agreed. I'll propose 10% credit for the spike window and share the SE notes. Thanks team.
Liam (SRE): Postmortem items: improve autoscale pre-warm for demo tenants, add capacity alarms at 60% burstpool, and document fallback behavior in POC runbook.
Ravi (Support): I'll capture logs for x-req-id=acme-req-3345 and attach to the CRM ticket.
Nora (Sales): Perfect — closing the loop with Acme in 15. :thumbsup:
